# pallet_xcm_bridge_hub - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/target-redirect/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/

## Expand description

Module that adds XCM support to bridge pallets. The pallet allows to dynamically open and close bridges between local (to this pallet location) and remote XCM destinations.

The `pallet_xcm_bridge_hub` pallet is used to manage (open, close) bridges between chains from
different consensuses. The new extrinsics `fn open_bridge` and `fn close_bridge` are introduced.
Other chains can manage channels with different bridged global consensuses.

[§](https://docs.rs#concept-of-lane-and-laneid)Concept of `lane` and `LaneId`

There is another `pallet_bridge_messages` pallet that handles inbound/outbound lanes for
messages. Each lane is a unique connection between two chains from different consensuses and is
identified by `LaneId`. `LaneId` is generated once when a new bridge is requested by `fn open_bridge`. It is generated by `BridgeLocations::calculate_lane_id` based on the following
parameters:

- Source `bridge_origin_universal_location`(latest XCM)
- Destination `bridge_destination_universal_location`(latest XCM)
- XCM version (both sides of the bridge must use the same parameters to generate the same
`LaneId`)- `bridge_origin_universal_location`,- `bridge_destination_universal_location`is converted to the- `Versioned*`structs

`LaneId` is expected to never change because:

- We need the same `LaneId`on both sides of the bridge, as`LaneId`is part of the message key proofs.
- Runtime upgrades are entirely asynchronous.
- We already have a running production Polkadot/Kusama bridge that uses `LaneId([0, 0, 0, 0])`.

`LaneId` is backward compatible, meaning it can be encoded/decoded from the older format `[u8; 4]` used for static lanes, as well as the new format `H256` generated by
`BridgeLocations::calculate_lane_id`.

[§](https://docs.rs#concept-of-bridge-and-bridgeid)Concept of `bridge` and `BridgeId`

The `pallet_xcm_bridge_hub` pallet needs to store some metadata about opened bridges. The bridge
(or bridge metadata) is stored under the `BridgeId` key.

`BridgeId` is generated from `bridge_origin_relative_location` and
`bridge_origin_universal_location` using the `latest` XCM structs. `BridgeId` is not transferred
over the bridge; it is only important for local consensus. It essentially serves as an index/key
to bridge metadata. All the XCM infrastructure around `XcmExecutor`, `SendXcm`, `ExportXcm` use
the `latest` XCM, so `BridgeId` must remain compatible with the `latest` XCM. For example, we
have an `ExportXcm` implementation in `exporter.rs` that handles the `ExportMessage` instruction
with `universal_source` and `destination` (latest XCM), so we need to create `BridgeId` and the
corresponding `LaneId`.

[§](https://docs.rs#migrations-and-state)Migrations and State

This pallet implements `try_state`, ensuring compatibility and checking everything so we know if
any migration is needed. `do_try_state` checks for `BridgeId` compatibility, which is
recalculated on runtime upgrade. Upgrading to a new XCM version should not break anything,
except removing older XCM versions. In such cases, we need to add migration for `BridgeId` and
stored `Versioned*` structs and update `LaneToBridge` mapping, but this won’t affect `LaneId`
over the bridge.

[§](https://docs.rs#how-to-open-a-bridge)How to Open a Bridge?

The `pallet_xcm_bridge_hub` pallet has the extrinsic `fn open_bridge` and an important
configuration `pallet_xcm_bridge_hub::Config::OpenBridgeOrigin`, which translates the call’s
origin to the XCM `Location` and converts it to the `bridge_origin_universal_location`. With the
current setup, this origin/location is expected to be either the relay chain or a sibling
parachain as one side of the bridge. Another parameter is
`bridge_destination_universal_location`, which is the other side of the bridge from a different
global consensus.

Every bridge between two XCM locations has a dedicated lane in associated messages pallet. Assuming that this pallet is deployed at the bridge hub parachain and there’s a similar pallet at the bridged network, the dynamic bridge lifetime is as follows:

-
the sibling parachain opens a XCMP channel with this bridge hub;
-
the sibling parachain funds its sovereign parachain account at this bridge hub. It shall hold enough funds to pay for the bridge (see `BridgeDeposit`);
-
the sibling parachain opens the bridge by sending XCM `Transact`instruction with the`open_bridge`call. The`BridgeDeposit`amount is reserved on the sovereign account of sibling parachain;
-
at the other side of the bridge, the same thing (1, 2, 3) happens. Parachains that need to connect over the bridge need to coordinate the moment when they start sending messages over the bridge. Otherwise they may lose messages and/or bundled assets;
-
when either side wants to close the bridge, it sends the XCM `Transact`with the`close_bridge`call. The bridge is closed immediately if there are no queued messages. Otherwise, the owner must repeat the`close_bridge`call to prune all queued messages first.

The pallet doesn’t provide any mechanism for graceful closure, because it always involves some contract between two connected chains and the bridge hub knows nothing about that. It is the task for the connected chains to make sure that all required actions are completed before the closure. In the end, the bridge hub can’t even guarantee that all messages that are delivered to the destination, are processed in the way their sender expects. So if we can’t guarantee that, we shall not care about more complex procedures and leave it to the participating parties.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Example of opening a bridge between some random parachains from Polkadot and Kusama:

- Let’s have:
- BridgeHubPolkadot with `UniversalLocation`=`[GlobalConsensus(Polkadot), Parachain(1002)]`
- BridgeHubKusama with `UniversalLocation`=`[GlobalConsensus(Kusama), Parachain(1002)]`

- BridgeHubPolkadot with
- The Polkadot local sibling parachain `Location::new(1, Parachain(1234))`must send some DOTs to its sovereign account on BridgeHubPolkadot to cover`BridgeDeposit`, fees for`Transact`, and the existential deposit.
- Send a call to the BridgeHubPolkadot from the local sibling parachain: `Location::new(1, Parachain(1234))``xcm::Transact( origin_kind: OriginKind::Xcm, XcmOverBridgeHubKusama::open_bridge( VersionedInteriorLocation::V4([GlobalConsensus(Kusama), Parachain(4567)].into()), ); )`
- Check the stored bridge metadata and generated `LaneId`.
- The Kusama local sibling parachain `Location::new(1, Parachain(4567))`must send some KSMs to its sovereign account on BridgeHubKusama to cover`BridgeDeposit`, fees for`Transact`, and the existential deposit.
- Send a call to the BridgeHubKusama from the local sibling parachain: `Location::new(1, Parachain(4567))``xcm::Transact( origin_kind: OriginKind::Xcm, XcmOverBridgeHubKusama::open_bridge( VersionedInteriorLocation::V4([GlobalConsensus(Polkadot), Parachain(1234)].into()), ); )`
- Check the stored bridge metadata and generated `LaneId`.
- Both `LaneId`s from steps 3 and 6 must be the same (see above*Concept of*).`lane`and`LaneId`
- Run the bridge messages relayer for `LaneId`.
- Send messages from both sides.

The opening bridge holds the configured `BridgeDeposit` from the origin’s sovereign account, but
this deposit is returned when the bridge is closed with `fn close_bridge`.

- Bridge identifier - used **only**for communicating with sibling/parent chains in the same consensus.

- An easy way to access `HaulBlobExporter`.
- [XcmAs](https://docs.rs/type.XcmAsPlainPayload.html)- Plain - Payload
- Encoded XCM blob. We expect the bridge messages pallet to use this blob type for both inbound and outbound payloads.

- Send a call to the BridgeHubPolkadot from the local sibling parachain: `Location::new(1, Parachain(1234))``xcm::Transact( origin_kind: OriginKind::Xcm, XcmOverBridgeHubKusama::open_bridge( VersionedInteriorLocation::V4([GlobalConsensus(Kusama), Parachain(4567)].into()), ); )`
- Check the stored bridge metadata and generated `LaneId`.
- The Kusama local sibling parachain `Location::new(1, Parachain(4567))`must send some KSMs to its sovereign account on BridgeHubKusama to cover`BridgeDeposit`, fees for`Transact`, and the existential deposit.
- Send a call to the BridgeHubKusama from the local sibling parachain: `Location::new(1, Parachain(4567))``xcm::Transact( origin_kind: OriginKind::Xcm, XcmOverBridgeHubKusama::open_bridge( VersionedInteriorLocation::V4([GlobalConsensus(Polkadot), Parachain(1234)].into()), ); )`
- Check the stored bridge metadata and generated `LaneId`.
- Both `LaneId`s from steps 3 and 6 must be the same (see above*Concept of*).`lane`and`LaneId`
- Run the bridge messages relayer for `LaneId`.
- Send messages from both sides.

The opening bridge holds the configured `BridgeDeposit` from the origin’s sovereign account, but
this deposit is returned when the bridge is closed with `fn close_bridge`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)::*;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [migration](https://docs.rs/migration/index.html)
- A module that is responsible for migration of storage.
- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)
- The `pallet`module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed to construct this pallet.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.Bridge.html)
- Bridge metadata.
- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeId.html)- Id
- Bridge identifier - used **only**for communicating with sibling/parent chains in the same consensus.
- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeLocations.html)- Locations
- Locations of bridge endpoints at both sides of the bridge.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/enum.BridgeState.html)- State
- Bridge state.
- [XcmBlob](https://docs.rs/enum.XcmBlobMessageDispatchResult.html)- Message - Dispatch - Result
- Message dispatch result type for single message.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [LOG_](https://docs.rs/constant.LOG_TARGET.html)- TARGET
- The target that will be used when publishing logs related to this pallet.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Local](https://docs.rs/trait.LocalXcmChannelManager.html)- XcmChannel - Manager
- Local XCM channel manager.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Pallet](https://docs.rs/type.PalletAsHaulBlobExporter.html)- AsHaul - Blob - Exporter
- An easy way to access `HaulBlobExporter`.
- [XcmAs](https://docs.rs/type.XcmAsPlainPayload.html)- Plain - Payload
- Encoded XCM blob. We expect the bridge messages pallet to use this blob type for both inbound and outbound payloads.

[298](#298)		#[pallet::weight(Weight::zero())] pub fn open_bridge(
[300](#300)			origin: OriginFor<T>,
[301](#301)			bridge_destination_universal_location: Box<VersionedInteriorLocation>,
[302](#302)		) -> DispatchResult {
[303](#303)			let xcm_version = bridge_destination_universal_location.identify_version();
[305](#305)			let locations =
[306](#306)				Self::bridge_locations_from_origin(origin, bridge_destination_universal_location)?;
[307](#307)			let lane_id = locations.calculate_lane_id(xcm_version).map_err(|e| {
[308](#308)				tracing::trace!(
[309](#309)					target: LOG_TARGET, error=?e,
[310](#310)					"calculate_lane_id error"
[311](#311)				);
[312](#312)				Error::<T, I>::BridgeLocations(e)
[313](#313)			})?;
[314](#314)
[315](#315)			Self::do_open_bridge(locations, lane_id, true)
[316](#316)		}
[317](#317)
[318](#318)		#[pallet::call_index(1)]
[336](#336)		#[pallet::weight(Weight::zero())] pub fn close_bridge(
[338](#338)			origin: OriginFor<T>,
[339](#339)			bridge_destination_universal_location: Box<VersionedInteriorLocation>,
[340](#340)			may_prune_messages: MessageNonce,
[341](#341)		) -> DispatchResult {
[342](#342)			let locations =
[344](#344)				Self::bridge_locations_from_origin(origin, bridge_destination_universal_location)?;
[345](#345)
[346](#346)			let bridge =
[351](#351)				Bridges::<T, I>::try_mutate_exists(locations.bridge_id(), |bridge| match bridge {
[352](#352)					Some(bridge) => {
[353](#353)						bridge.state = BridgeState::Closed;
[354](#354)						Ok(bridge.clone())
[355](#355)					},
[356](#356)					None => Err(Error::<T, I>::UnknownBridge),
[357](#357)				})?;
[358](#358)
[359](#359)			let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<T, I>::new();
[361](#361)			let mut inbound_lane = lanes_manager
[362](#362)				.any_state_inbound_lane(bridge.lane_id)
[363](#363)				.map_err(Error::<T, I>::LanesManager)?;
[364](#364)			let mut outbound_lane = lanes_manager
[365](#365)				.any_state_outbound_lane(bridge.lane_id)
[366](#366)				.map_err(Error::<T, I>::LanesManager)?;
[367](#367)
[368](#368)			let mut pruned_messages = 0;
[370](#370)			for _ in outbound_lane.queued_messages() {
[371](#371)				if pruned_messages == may_prune_messages {
[372](#372)					break;
[373](#373)				}
[374](#374)
[375](#375)				outbound_lane.remove_oldest_unpruned_message();
[376](#376)				pruned_messages += 1;
[377](#377)			}
[378](#378)
[379](#379)			if !outbound_lane.queued_messages().is_empty() {
[381](#381)				inbound_lane.set_state(LaneState::Closed);
[383](#383)				outbound_lane.set_state(LaneState::Closed);
[384](#384)
[385](#385)				let enqueued_messages = outbound_lane.queued_messages().saturating_len();
[387](#387)				tracing::trace!(
[388](#388)					target: LOG_TARGET,
[389](#389)					bridge_id=?locations.bridge_id(),
[390](#390)					bridge_origin=?locations.bridge_origin_universal_location(),
[391](#391)					bridge_destination=?locations.bridge_destination_universal_location(),
[392](#392)					lane_id=?bridge.lane_id,
[393](#393)					messages_remaining=%enqueued_messages,
[394](#394)					"Bridge is closing."
[395](#395)				);
[396](#396)
[397](#397)				Self::deposit_event(Event::<T, I>::ClosingBridge {
[399](#399)					bridge_id: *locations.bridge_id(),
[400](#400)					lane_id: bridge.lane_id.into(),
[401](#401)					pruned_messages,
[402](#402)					enqueued_messages,
[403](#403)				});
[404](#404)
[405](#405)				return Ok(());
[406](#406)			}
[407](#407)
[408](#408)			inbound_lane.purge();
[410](#410)			outbound_lane.purge();
[411](#411)			Bridges::<T, I>::remove(locations.bridge_id());
[412](#412)			LaneToBridge::<T, I>::remove(bridge.lane_id);
[413](#413)
[414](#414)			let released_deposit = T::Currency::release(
[416](#416)				&HoldReason::BridgeDeposit.into(),
[417](#417)				&bridge.bridge_owner_account,
[418](#418)				bridge.deposit,
[419](#419)				Precision::BestEffort,
[420](#420)			)
[421](#421)			.inspect_err(|e| {
[422](#422)				tracing::error!(
[425](#425)					target: LOG_TARGET,
[426](#426)					error=?e,
[427](#427)					bridge_id=?locations.bridge_id(),
[428](#428)					"Failed to unreserve during the bridge closure"
[429](#429)				);
[430](#430)			})
[431](#431)			.ok()
[432](#432)			.unwrap_or(BalanceOf::<ThisChainOf<T, I>>::zero());
[433](#433)
[434](#434)			tracing::trace!(
[436](#436)				target: LOG_TARGET,
[437](#437)				bridge_id=?locations.bridge_id(),
[438](#438)				bridge_origin=?locations.bridge_origin_universal_location(),
[439](#439)				bridge_destination=?locations.bridge_destination_universal_location(),
[440](#440)				lane_id=?bridge.lane_id,
[441](#441)				bridge_deposit=?released_deposit,
[442](#442)				"Bridge has closed, the bridge deposit was returned"
[443](#443)			);
[444](#444)
[445](#445)			Self::deposit_event(Event::<T, I>::BridgePruned {
[447](#447)				bridge_id: *locations.bridge_id(),
[448](#448)				lane_id: bridge.lane_id.into(),
[449](#449)				bridge_deposit: released_deposit,
[450](#450)				pruned_messages,
[451](#451)			});
[452](#452)
[453](#453)			Ok(())
[454](#454)		}
[455](#455)	}
[456](#456)
[457](#457)	impl<T: Config<I>, I: 'static> Pallet<T, I> {
[458](#458)		pub fn do_open_bridge(
[460](#460)			locations: Box<BridgeLocations>,
[461](#461)			lane_id: T::LaneId,
[462](#462)			create_lanes: bool,
[463](#463)		) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {
[464](#464)			let bridge_owner_account = T::BridgeOriginAccountIdConverter::convert_location(
[466](#466)				locations.bridge_origin_relative_location(),
[467](#467)			)
[468](#468)			.ok_or(Error::<T, I>::InvalidBridgeOriginAccount)?;
[469](#469)			let deposit = if T::AllowWithoutBridgeDeposit::contains(
[470](#470)				locations.bridge_origin_relative_location(),
[471](#471)			) {
[472](#472)				BalanceOf::<ThisChainOf<T, I>>::zero()
[473](#473)			} else {
[474](#474)				let deposit = T::BridgeDeposit::get();
[475](#475)				T::Currency::hold(
[476](#476)					&HoldReason::BridgeDeposit.into(),
[477](#477)					&bridge_owner_account,
[478](#478)					deposit,
[479](#479)				)
[480](#480)				.map_err(|e| {
[481](#481)					tracing::error!(
[482](#482)						target: LOG_TARGET,
[483](#483)						error=?e,
[484](#484)						?deposit,
[485](#485)						?bridge_owner_account,
[486](#486)						bridge_origin_relative_location=?locations.bridge_origin_relative_location(),
[487](#487)						"Failed to hold bridge deposit"
[488](#488)					);
[489](#489)					Error::<T, I>::FailedToReserveBridgeDeposit
[490](#490)				})?;
[491](#491)				deposit
[492](#492)			};
[493](#493)
[494](#494)			Bridges::<T, I>::try_mutate(locations.bridge_id(), |bridge| match bridge {
[496](#496)				Some(_) => Err(Error::<T, I>::BridgeAlreadyExists),
[497](#497)				None => {
[498](#498)					*bridge = Some(BridgeOf::<T, I> {
[499](#499)						bridge_origin_relative_location: Box::new(
[500](#500)							locations.bridge_origin_relative_location().clone().into(),
[501](#501)						),
[502](#502)						bridge_origin_universal_location: Box::new(
[503](#503)							locations.bridge_origin_universal_location().clone().into(),
[504](#504)						),
[505](#505)						bridge_destination_universal_location: Box::new(
[506](#506)							locations.bridge_destination_universal_location().clone().into(),
[507](#507)						),
[508](#508)						state: BridgeState::Opened,
[509](#509)						bridge_owner_account,
[510](#510)						deposit,
[511](#511)						lane_id,
[512](#512)					});
[513](#513)					Ok(())
[514](#514)				},
[515](#515)			})?;
[516](#516)			LaneToBridge::<T, I>::try_mutate(lane_id, |bridge| match bridge {
[518](#518)				Some(_) => Err(Error::<T, I>::BridgeAlreadyExists),
[519](#519)				None => {
[520](#520)					*bridge = Some(*locations.bridge_id());
[521](#521)					Ok(())
[522](#522)				},
[523](#523)			})?;
[524](#524)
[525](#525)			if create_lanes {
[526](#526)				let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<T, I>::new();
[528](#528)				lanes_manager
[529](#529)					.create_inbound_lane(lane_id)
[530](#530)					.map_err(Error::<T, I>::LanesManager)?;
[531](#531)				lanes_manager
[532](#532)					.create_outbound_lane(lane_id)
[533](#533)					.map_err(Error::<T, I>::LanesManager)?;
[534](#534)			}
[535](#535)
[536](#536)			tracing::trace!(
[538](#538)				target: LOG_TARGET,
[539](#539)				bridge_id=?locations.bridge_id(),
[540](#540)				bridge_origin=?locations.bridge_origin_universal_location(),
[541](#541)				bridge_destination=?locations.bridge_destination_universal_location(),
[542](#542)				lane_id=?lane_id,
[543](#543)				"Bridge has been opened"
[544](#544)			);
[545](#545)
[546](#546)			Self::deposit_event(Event::<T, I>::BridgeOpened {
[548](#548)				bridge_id: *locations.bridge_id(),
[549](#549)				bridge_deposit: deposit,
[550](#550)				local_endpoint: Box::new(locations.bridge_origin_universal_location().clone()),
[551](#551)				remote_endpoint: Box::new(
[552](#552)					locations.bridge_destination_universal_location().clone(),
[553](#553)				),
[554](#554)				lane_id: lane_id.into(),
[555](#555)			});
[556](#556)
[557](#557)			Ok(())
[558](#558)		}
[559](#559)	}

[608](#608)
[609](#609)	impl<T: Config<I>, I: 'static> Pallet<T, I> {
[610](#610)		fn bridged_network_id() -> Result<NetworkId, sp_runtime::DispatchError> {
[612](#612)			match T::BridgedNetwork::get().take_first_interior() {
[613](#613)				Some(GlobalConsensus(network)) => Ok(network),
[614](#614)				_ => Err(Error::<T, I>::BridgeLocations(
[615](#615)					BridgeLocationsError::InvalidBridgeDestination,
[616](#616)				)
[617](#617)				.into()),
[618](#618)			}
[619](#619)		}
[620](#620)	}
[621](#621)
[622](#622)	#[cfg(any(test, feature = "try-runtime", feature = "std"))]
[623](#623)	impl<T: Config<I>, I: 'static> Pallet<T, I> {
[624](#624)		pub fn do_try_state() -> Result<(), sp_runtime::TryRuntimeError> {
[626](#626)			use sp_std::collections::btree_set::BTreeSet;
[627](#627)
[628](#628)			let mut lanes = BTreeSet::new();
[629](#629)
[630](#630)			for (bridge_id, bridge) in Bridges::<T, I>::iter() {
[632](#632)				lanes.insert(Self::do_try_state_for_bridge(bridge_id, bridge)?);
[633](#633)			}
[634](#634)			ensure!(
[635](#635)				lanes.len() == Bridges::<T, I>::iter().count(),
[636](#636)				"Invalid `Bridges` configuration, probably two bridges handle the same laneId!"
[637](#637)			);
[638](#638)			ensure!(
[639](#639)				lanes.len() == LaneToBridge::<T, I>::iter().count(),
[640](#640)				"Invalid `LaneToBridge` configuration, probably missing or not removed laneId!"
[641](#641)			);
[642](#642)
[643](#643)			Self::do_try_state_for_messages()
[645](#645)		}
[646](#646)
[647](#647)		pub fn do_try_state_for_bridge(
[649](#649)			bridge_id: BridgeId,
[650](#650)			bridge: BridgeOf<T, I>,
[651](#651)		) -> Result<T::LaneId, sp_runtime::TryRuntimeError> {
[652](#652)			tracing::info!(target: LOG_TARGET, ?bridge_id, ?bridge, "Checking `do_try_state_for_bridge`");
[653](#653)
[654](#654)			ensure!(
[656](#656)				Some(bridge_id) == LaneToBridge::<T, I>::get(bridge.lane_id),
[657](#657)				"Found `LaneToBridge` inconsistency for bridge_id - missing mapping!"
[658](#658)			);
[659](#659)
[660](#660)			let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<T, I>::new();
[662](#662)			ensure!(
[663](#663)				lanes_manager.any_state_inbound_lane(bridge.lane_id).is_ok(),
[664](#664)				"Inbound lane not found!",
[665](#665)			);
[666](#666)			ensure!(
[667](#667)				lanes_manager.any_state_outbound_lane(bridge.lane_id).is_ok(),
[668](#668)				"Outbound lane not found!",
[669](#669)			);
[670](#670)
[671](#671)			let bridge_origin_relative_location_as_latest: &Location = &(*bridge.bridge_origin_relative_location).try_into()
[673](#673)				.map_err(|_| "`bridge.bridge_origin_relative_location` cannot be converted to the `latest` XCM, needs migration!")?;
[674](#674)			let bridge_origin_universal_location_as_latest: &InteriorLocation = &(*bridge.bridge_origin_universal_location).try_into()
[675](#675)				.map_err(|_| "`bridge.bridge_origin_universal_location` cannot be converted to the `latest` XCM, needs migration!")?;
[676](#676)			let bridge_destination_universal_location_as_latest: &InteriorLocation = &(*bridge.bridge_destination_universal_location).try_into()
[677](#677)				.map_err(|_| "`bridge.bridge_destination_universal_location` cannot be converted to the `latest` XCM, needs migration!")?;
[678](#678)
[679](#679)			ensure!(
[681](#681)				bridge_id == BridgeId::new(bridge_origin_universal_location_as_latest, bridge_destination_universal_location_as_latest),
[682](#682)				"`bridge_id` is different than calculated from `bridge_origin_universal_location_as_latest` and `bridge_destination_universal_location_as_latest`, needs migration!"
[683](#683)			);
[684](#684)
[685](#685)			ensure!(
[687](#687)				T::BridgeOriginAccountIdConverter::convert_location(bridge_origin_relative_location_as_latest) == Some(bridge.bridge_owner_account),
[688](#688)				"`bridge.bridge_owner_account` is different than calculated from `bridge.bridge_origin_relative_location`, needs migration!"
[689](#689)			);
[690](#690)
[691](#691)			Ok(bridge.lane_id)
[692](#692)		}
[693](#693)
[694](#694)		pub fn do_try_state_for_messages() -> Result<(), sp_runtime::TryRuntimeError> {
[696](#696)			for lane_id in pallet_bridge_messages::InboundLanes::<T, T::BridgeMessagesPalletInstance>::iter_keys() {
[698](#698)				tracing::info!(target: LOG_TARGET, ?lane_id, "Checking `do_try_state_for_messages` for `InboundLanes`...");
[699](#699)				ensure!(
[700](#700)					LaneToBridge::<T, I>::get(lane_id).is_some(),
[701](#701)					"Found `LaneToBridge` inconsistency for `InboundLanes`'s lane_id - missing mapping!"
[702](#702)				);
[703](#703)			}
[704](#704)
[705](#705)			for lane_id in pallet_bridge_messages::OutboundLanes::<T, T::BridgeMessagesPalletInstance>::iter_keys() {
[707](#707)				tracing::info!(target: LOG_TARGET, ?lane_id, "Checking `do_try_state_for_messages` for `OutboundLanes`");
[708](#708)				ensure!(
[709](#709)					LaneToBridge::<T, I>::get(lane_id).is_some(),
[710](#710)					"Found `LaneToBridge` inconsistency for `OutboundLanes`'s lane_id - missing mapping!"
[711](#711)				);
[712](#712)			}
[713](#713)
[714](#714)			Ok(())
[715](#715)		}
[716](#716)	}
[717](#717)

[736](#736)		#[serde(skip)]

[739](#739)	}
[740](#740)
[741](#741)	#[pallet::genesis_build]
[742](#742)	impl<T: Config<I>, I: 'static> BuildGenesisConfig for GenesisConfig<T, I>
[743](#743)	where
[744](#744)		T: frame_system::Config<AccountId = AccountIdOf<ThisChainOf<T, I>>>,
[745](#745)	{
[746](#746)		fn build(&self) {
[747](#747)			for (
[748](#748)				bridge_origin_relative_location,
[749](#749)				bridge_destination_universal_location,
[750](#750)				maybe_lane_id,
[751](#751)			) in &self.opened_bridges
[752](#752)			{
[753](#753)				let locations = Pallet::<T, I>::bridge_locations(
[754](#754)					bridge_origin_relative_location.clone(),
[755](#755)					bridge_destination_universal_location.clone().into(),
[756](#756)				)
[757](#757)				.expect("Invalid genesis configuration");
[758](#758)
[759](#759)				let lane_id = match maybe_lane_id {
[760](#760)					Some(lane_id) => *lane_id,
[761](#761)					None => {
[762](#762)						locations.calculate_lane_id(xcm::latest::VERSION).expect("Valid locations")
[763](#763)					},
[764](#764)				};
[765](#765)
[766](#766)				Pallet::<T, I>::do_open_bridge(locations, lane_id, true)
[767](#767)					.expect("Valid opened bridge!");
[768](#768)			}
[769](#769)		}
[770](#770)	}

[1094](#1094)	#[test]
[1095](#1095)	fn open_bridge_works() {
[1096](#1096)		run_test(|| {
[1097](#1097)			let origins = [
[1100](#1100)				(OpenBridgeOrigin::parent_relay_chain_origin(), 0),
[1101](#1101)				(OpenBridgeOrigin::sibling_parachain_origin(), BridgeDeposit::get()),
[1102](#1102)			];
[1103](#1103)
[1104](#1104)			let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<TestRuntime, ()>::new();
[1106](#1106)			let existential_deposit = ExistentialDeposit::get();
[1107](#1107)			for (origin, expected_deposit) in origins {
[1108](#1108)				System::set_block_number(1);

[1118](#1118)							.into_version(xcm_version)
[1119](#1119)							.expect("valid conversion"),
[1120](#1120)					),
[1121](#1121)				)

[1141](#1141)				);

[1444](#1444)	#[test]
[1445](#1445)	fn do_try_state_works() {
[1446](#1446)		let bridge_origin_relative_location = SiblingLocation::get();
[1447](#1447)		let bridge_origin_universal_location = SiblingUniversalLocation::get();
[1448](#1448)		let bridge_destination_universal_location = BridgedUniversalDestination::get();
[1449](#1449)		let bridge_owner_account =
[1450](#1450)			LocationToAccountId::convert_location(&bridge_origin_relative_location)
[1451](#1451)				.expect("valid accountId");
[1452](#1452)		let bridge_owner_account_mismatch =
[1453](#1453)			LocationToAccountId::convert_location(&Location::parent()).expect("valid accountId");
[1454](#1454)		let bridge_id = BridgeId::new(
[1455](#1455)			&bridge_origin_universal_location,
[1456](#1456)			&bridge_destination_universal_location,
[1457](#1457)		);
[1458](#1458)		let bridge_id_mismatch = BridgeId::new(&InteriorLocation::Here, &InteriorLocation::Here);
[1459](#1459)		let lane_id = TestLaneIdType::try_new(1, 2).unwrap();
[1460](#1460)		let lane_id_mismatch = TestLaneIdType::try_new(3, 4).unwrap();
[1461](#1461)
[1462](#1462)		let test_bridge_state =
[1463](#1463)			|id,
[1464](#1464)			 bridge,
[1465](#1465)			 (lane_id, bridge_id),
[1466](#1466)			 (inbound_lane_id, outbound_lane_id),
[1467](#1467)			 expected_error: Option<TryRuntimeError>| {
[1468](#1468)				Bridges::<TestRuntime, ()>::insert(id, bridge);
[1469](#1469)				LaneToBridge::<TestRuntime, ()>::insert(lane_id, bridge_id);
[1470](#1470)
[1471](#1471)				let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<TestRuntime, ()>::new();
[1472](#1472)				lanes_manager.create_inbound_lane(inbound_lane_id).unwrap();
[1473](#1473)				lanes_manager.create_outbound_lane(outbound_lane_id).unwrap();
[1474](#1474)
[1475](#1475)				let result = XcmOverBridge::do_try_state();
[1476](#1476)				if let Some(e) = expected_error {
[1477](#1477)					assert_err!(result, e);
[1478](#1478)				} else {
[1479](#1479)					assert_ok!(result);
[1480](#1480)				}
[1481](#1481)			};
[1482](#1482)		let cleanup = |bridge_id, lane_ids| {
[1483](#1483)			Bridges::<TestRuntime, ()>::remove(bridge_id);
[1484](#1484)			for lane_id in lane_ids {
[1485](#1485)				LaneToBridge::<TestRuntime, ()>::remove(lane_id);
[1486](#1486)				let lanes_manager = LanesManagerOf::<TestRuntime, ()>::new();
[1487](#1487)				if let Ok(lane) = lanes_manager.any_state_inbound_lane(lane_id) {
[1488](#1488)					lane.purge();
[1489](#1489)				}
[1490](#1490)				if let Ok(lane) = lanes_manager.any_state_outbound_lane(lane_id) {
[1491](#1491)					lane.purge();
[1492](#1492)				}
[1493](#1493)			}
[1494](#1494)			assert_ok!(XcmOverBridge::do_try_state());
[1495](#1495)		};
[1496](#1496)
[1497](#1497)		run_test(|| {
[1498](#1498)			test_bridge_state(
[1500](#1500)				bridge_id,
[1501](#1501)				Bridge {
[1502](#1502)					bridge_origin_relative_location: Box::new(VersionedLocation::from(
[1503](#1503)						bridge_origin_relative_location.clone(),
[1504](#1504)					)),
[1505](#1505)					bridge_origin_universal_location: Box::new(VersionedInteriorLocation::from(
[1506](#1506)						bridge_origin_universal_location.clone(),
[1507](#1507)					)),
[1508](#1508)					bridge_destination_universal_location: Box::new(
[1509](#1509)						VersionedInteriorLocation::from(
[1510](#1510)							bridge_destination_universal_location.clone(),
[1511](#1511)						),
[1512](#1512)					),
[1513](#1513)					state: BridgeState::Opened,
[1514](#1514)					bridge_owner_account: bridge_owner_account.clone(),
[1515](#1515)					deposit: Zero::zero(),
[1516](#1516)					lane_id,
[1517](#1517)				},
[1518](#1518)				(lane_id, bridge_id),
[1519](#1519)				(lane_id, lane_id),
[1520](#1520)				None,
[1521](#1521)			);
[1522](#1522)			cleanup(bridge_id, vec![lane_id]);
[1523](#1523)
[1524](#1524)			test_bridge_state(
[1526](#1526)				bridge_id,
[1527](#1527)				Bridge {
[1528](#1528)					bridge_origin_relative_location: Box::new(VersionedLocation::from(
[1529](#1529)						bridge_origin_relative_location.clone(),
[1530](#1530)					)),
[1531](#1531)					bridge_origin_universal_location: Box::new(VersionedInteriorLocation::from(
[1532](#1532)						bridge_origin_universal_location.clone(),
[1533](#1533)					)),
[1534](#1534)					bridge_destination_universal_location: Box::new(
[1535](#1535)						VersionedInteriorLocation::from(
[1536](#1536)							bridge_destination_universal_location.clone(),
[1537](#1537)						),
[1538](#1538)					),
[1539](#1539)					state: BridgeState::Opened,
[1540](#1540)					bridge_owner_account: bridge_owner_account.clone(),
[1541](#1541)					deposit: Zero::zero(),
[1542](#1542)					lane_id,
[1543](#1543)				},
[1544](#1544)				(lane_id, bridge_id_mismatch),
[1545](#1545)				(lane_id, lane_id),
[1546](#1546)				Some(TryRuntimeError::Other(
[1547](#1547)					"Found `LaneToBridge` inconsistency for bridge_id - missing mapping!",
[1548](#1548)				)),
[1549](#1549)			);
[1550](#1550)			cleanup(bridge_id, vec![lane_id]);
[1551](#1551)
[1552](#1552)			test_bridge_state(
[1554](#1554)				bridge_id,
[1555](#1555)				Bridge {
[1556](#1556)					bridge_origin_relative_location: Box::new(VersionedLocation::from(

# pallet_xcm_bridge_hub::pallet - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/pallet/index.html

## Expand description

The `pallet` module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed
to construct this pallet.

The main components of this pallet are:

- `Pallet`- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
`dispatchables``Call`

- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
- `storage_types`- *Type Definitions*
- `Config`
- `Event`- `Error`- *Enums*

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [dispatchables](https://docs.rs/dispatchables/index.html)
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all defined dispatchables for this pallet.
- [storage_](https://docs.rs/storage_types/index.html)- types
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all (public and private) defined storage types for this pallet.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Genesis](https://docs.rs/struct.GenesisConfig.html)- Config
- Can be used to configure the
[genesis state](https://docs.substrate.io/build/genesis-configuration/)of this pallet.
- [Instance1](https://docs.rs/struct.Instance1.html)
- `Instance1`to be used for instantiable pallets defined with the- `#[pallet]`
- [Pallet](https://docs.rs/struct.Pallet.html)
- The `Pallet`struct, the main type that implements traits and standalone functions within the pallet.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.Call.html)
- Contains a variant per dispatchable extrinsic that this pallet has.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- The `Error`enum of this pallet.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/enum.Event.html)
- The `Event`enum of this pallet
- [Hold](https://docs.rs/enum.HoldReason.html)- Reason
- The reason for this pallet placing a hold on funds.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.Config.html)
- Configuration trait of this pallet.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/type.BridgeOf.html)- Of
- An alias for the bridge metadata.
- [Bridges](https://docs.rs/type.Bridges.html)
- All registered bridges.
- [Lane](https://docs.rs/type.LaneIdOf.html)- IdOf
- An alias for lane identifier type.
- [Lane](https://docs.rs/type.LaneToBridge.html)- ToBridge
- All registered `lane_id`and`bridge_id`mappings.
- [Lanes](https://docs.rs/type.LanesManagerOf.html)- Manager - Of
- An alias for the associated lanes manager.
- [Module](https://docs.rs/type.Module.html)- Deprecated
- Type alias to `Pallet`, to be used by`construct_runtime`.
- [This](https://docs.rs/type.ThisChainOf.html)- Chain - Of
- An alias for this chain.

# pallet_xcm_bridge_hub::migration - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/migration/index.html

## Expand description

A module that is responsible for migration of storage.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenBridgeForLane.html)- Bridge - ForLane
- This migration does not modify storage but can be used to open a bridge and link it to the
specified LaneId. This is useful when we want to open a bridge and use a custom LaneId instead
of the pre-calculated one provided by the `fn open_bridge extrinsic`. Or perhaps if you want to ensure that your runtime (e.g., for testing) always has an open bridge.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [STORAGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.STORAGE_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- The in-code storage version.

---

Bridge metadata.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.bridge_origin_relative_location)

`bridge_origin_relative_location: `[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[VersionedLocation](https://docs.rs/staging-xcm/24.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/staging_xcm/enum.VersionedLocation.html)>Relative location of the bridge origin chain. This is expected to be **convertible** to the
`latest` XCM, so the check and migration needs to be ensured.

---

# BridgeId in pallet_xcm_bridge_hub - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/struct.BridgeId.html

`pub struct BridgeId(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

Bridge identifier - used **only** for communicating with sibling/parent chains in the same
consensus.

For example, `SendXcm` implementations (which use the `latest` XCM) can use it to identify a
bridge and the corresponding `LaneId` that is used for over-consensus communication between
bridge hubs.

This identifier is constructed from the `latest` XCM, so it is expected to ensure migration to
the `latest` XCM version. This could change the `BridgeId`, but it will not affect the `LaneId`.
In other words, `LaneId` will never change, while `BridgeId` could change with (every) XCM
upgrade.

# BridgeState in pallet_xcm_bridge_hub - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/enum.BridgeState.html

```
pub enum BridgeState {
    Opened,
    Suspended,
    Closed,
}
```
## Expand description

Bridge state.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Opened)

### Opened

Bridge is opened. Associated lanes are also opened.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Suspended)

### Suspended

Bridge is suspended. Associated lanes are opened.

We keep accepting messages to the bridge. The only difference with the `Opened` state
is that we have sent the “Suspended” message/signal to the local bridge origin.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Closed)

### Closed

Bridge is closed. Associated lanes are also closed. After all outbound messages will be pruned, the bridge will vanish without any traces.

# XcmBlobMessageDispatchResult in pallet_xcm_bridge_hub - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-xcm-bridge-hub/0.25.0/pallet_xcm_bridge_hub/enum.XcmBlobMessageDispatchResult.html

```
pub enum XcmBlobMessageDispatchResult {
    InvalidPayload,
    Dispatched,
    NotDispatched(
```
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[DispatchBlobError](https://docs.rs/staging-xcm-builder/29.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/staging_xcm_builder/universal_exports/enum.DispatchBlobError.html)>),
}## Expand description

Message dispatch result type for single message.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPayload)

### InvalidPayload

We’ve been unable to decode message payload.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Dispatched)

### Dispatched

Message has been dispatched.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotDispatched)

### NotDispatched([Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[DispatchBlobError](https://docs.rs/staging-xcm-builder/29.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/staging_xcm_builder/universal_exports/enum.DispatchBlobError.html)>)

Message has **NOT** been dispatched because of given error.

# overseerd-hooks 0.9.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/overseerd-hooks/0.9.0

A general lifecycle/event **hook** system.

A hook is an `async` method on a component or service, marked `#[hook(Kind)]`, that the
framework calls when an event of `Kind` occurs. `Kind` is a [`HookKind`] type that owns
the hook's *output* (what the method returns) and its *context* (the typed inputs an
invocation carries). Built-in kinds are [`Startup`] and [`Shutdown`]; config reload is a
kind defined in `overseerd-config`. The system is deliberately general so user-defined
event kinds can be added the same way.

Hooks do **not** receive component dependencies as parameters — those are reached through
`&self` (a hook may also be self-less). A hook's only parameters are the kind's inputs,
each a [`HookParam`] extracted from the kind's context. Hooks are collected per type
(the `{Type}Hooks` distributed slice, exposed via [`ComponentHooks`]) and registered into
a [`HookManager`]; a type with no hooks contributes nothing at runtime.

This crate is generic over the [ ResolverCtx](https://docs.rs/overseerd_core::ResolverCtx): a hook's
erased [

`HookCall`] resolves its receiver through the resolver context, so the hook
layer never names the DI container (which sits above it).

---

# futures - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures/^0.3/

## Expand description

Abstractions for asynchronous programming.

This crate provides a number of core abstractions for writing asynchronous code:

- [Futures](https://docs.rs/future/index.html)are single eventual values produced by asynchronous computations. Some programming languages (e.g. JavaScript) call this concept “promise”.
- [Streams](https://docs.rs/stream/index.html)represent a series of values produced asynchronously.
- [Sinks](https://docs.rs/sink/index.html)provide support for asynchronous writing of data.
- [Executors](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)are responsible for running asynchronous tasks.

The crate also contains abstractions for [asynchronous I/O](https://docs.rs/io/index.html) and
[cross-task communication](https://docs.rs/channel/index.html).

Underlying all of this is the *task system*, which is a form of lightweight
threading. Large asynchronous computations are built up using futures,
streams and sinks, and then spawned as independent tasks that are run to
completion, but *do not block* the thread running them.

The following example describes how the task system context is built and used within macros and keywords such as async and await!.

```
fn main() {
    let pool = ThreadPool::new().expect("Failed to build pool");
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded::<i32>();
    // Create a future by an async block, where async is responsible for an
    // implementation of Future. At this point no executor has been provided
    // to this future, so it will not be running.
    let fut_values = async {
        // Create another async block, again where the Future implementation
        // is generated by async. Since this is inside of a parent async block,
        // it will be provided with the executor of the parent block when the parent
        // block is executed.
        //
        // This executor chaining is done by Future::poll whose second argument
        // is a std::task::Context. This represents our executor, and the Future
        // implemented by this async block can be polled using the parent async
        // block's executor.
        let fut_tx_result = async move {
            (0..100).for_each(|v| {
                tx.unbounded_send(v).expect("Failed to send");
            })
        };
        // Use the provided thread pool to spawn the generated future
        // responsible for transmission
        pool.spawn_ok(fut_tx_result);
        let fut_values = rx
            .map(|v| v * 2)
            .collect();
        // Use the executor provided to this async block to wait for the
        // future to complete.
        fut_values.await
    };
    // Actually execute the above future, which will invoke Future::poll and
    // subsequently chain appropriate Future::poll and methods needing executors
    // to drive all futures. Eventually fut_values will be driven to completion.
    let values: Vec<i32> = executor::block_on(fut_values);
    println!("Values={:?}", values);
}
```
The majority of examples and code snippets in this crate assume that they are inside an async block as written above.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, returning a tuple of all results once complete.
- [pending](https://docs.rs/macro.pending.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which yields to the event loop once.
- [pin_mut](https://docs.rs/macro.pin_mut.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [poll](https://docs.rs/macro.poll.html)- `async-await`
- A macro which returns the result of polling a future once within the
current `async`context.
- [ready](https://docs.rs/macro.ready.html)
- Extracts the successful type of `Poll<T>`.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `async-await`and- `std`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. If multiple futures are ready,
one will be pseudo-randomly selected at runtime. Futures directly
passed to `select!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [select_](https://docs.rs/macro.select_biased.html)- biased - `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures and streams simultaneously, executing the branch
for the future that finishes first. Unlike `select!``select_biased!`must be`Unpin`and implement`FusedFuture`.
- [stream_](https://docs.rs/macro.stream_select.html)- select - `async-await`and- `std`
- Combines several streams, all producing the same `Item`type, into one stream. This is similar to`select_all`but does not require the streams to all be the same type. It also keeps the streams inline, and does not require`Box<dyn Stream>`s to be allocated. Streams passed to this macro must be`Unpin`.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `async-await`
- Polls multiple futures simultaneously, resolving to a `Result`

---

# overseerd_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-core/^0.9.0/

## Expand description

Leaf vocabulary for the Overseerd framework.

This crate is the bottom of the dependency graph: it depends on nothing internal and
everything else depends on it. It defines the shared *language* the layers above
speak — type descriptors, the dependency-edge model, component scopes, the by-type
[ Descriptor](https://docs.rs/descriptor/trait.Descriptor.html) seam — and the

[abstraction through which all dependency resolution flows.](https://docs.rs/resolver/index.html)

`resolver`It contains no runtime, no container, no config, and no protocol code. Those live in
`overseerd-di`, `overseerd-config`, `overseerd-hooks`, and `overseerd-daemon`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use dependency::`- [Cardinality](https://docs.rs/dependency/enum.Cardinality.html);
- `pub use dependency::`- [DependencyDescriptor](https://docs.rs/dependency/struct.DependencyDescriptor.html);
- `pub use descriptor::`- [Descriptor](https://docs.rs/descriptor/trait.Descriptor.html);
- `pub use resolver::`- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/resolver/trait.Resolver.html);
- `pub use resolver::`- [ResolverCtx](https://docs.rs/resolver/trait.ResolverCtx.html);
- `pub use resolver::`- [ResolverCtxExt](https://docs.rs/resolver/trait.ResolverCtxExt.html);
- `pub use resolver::`- [ResolverSet](https://docs.rs/resolver/struct.ResolverSet.html);
- `pub use scope::`- [Scope](https://docs.rs/scope/trait.Scope.html);
- `pub use scope::`- [Singleton](https://docs.rs/scope/struct.Singleton.html);
- `pub use scope::`- [StaticScope](https://docs.rs/scope/trait.StaticScope.html);

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^2/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

---

# overseerd_hooks - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/overseerd-hooks/0.9.0/target-redirect/overseerd_hooks/

## Expand description

A general lifecycle/event **hook** system.

A hook is an `async` method on a component or service, marked `#[hook(Kind)]`, that the
framework calls when an event of `Kind` occurs. `Kind` is a [ HookKind](https://docs.rs/trait.HookKind.html) type that owns
the hook’s

*output*(what the method returns) and its

*context*(the typed inputs an invocation carries). Built-in kinds are

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Startup.html)

`Startup`[; config reload is a kind defined in](https://docs.rs/struct.Shutdown.html)

`Shutdown``overseerd-config`. The system is deliberately general so user-defined
event kinds can be added the same way.Hooks do **not** receive component dependencies as parameters — those are reached through
`&self` (a hook may also be self-less). A hook’s only parameters are the kind’s inputs,
each a [ HookParam](https://docs.rs/trait.HookParam.html) extracted from the kind’s context. Hooks are collected per type
(the

`{Type}Hooks` distributed slice, exposed via [) and registered into a](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentHooks.html)

`ComponentHooks`[; a type with no hooks contributes nothing at runtime.](https://docs.rs/struct.HookManager.html)

`HookManager`This crate is generic over the [ ResolverCtx](https://docs.rs/overseerd-core/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_core/resolver/trait.ResolverCtx.html): a hook’s
erased

[resolves its receiver through the resolver context, so the hook layer never names the DI container (which sits above it).](https://docs.rs/type.HookCall.html)

`HookCall`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata for one hook, registered into its type’s `{Type}Hooks`slice.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookManager.html)- Manager
- Runs hooks of a kind against the live component instances.
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.Shutdown.html)
- Fired once when the daemon begins a graceful shutdown (the serve/run loop has stopped).
Errors from a `#[hook(Shutdown)]`are logged; shutdown proceeds regardless.
- [Startup](https://docs.rs/struct.Startup.html)
- Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving. An `Err`from any`#[hook(Startup)]`aborts startup — the daemon does not begin accepting work.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors from running a hook: framework failures only. A hook’s *domain*outcome (e.g. whether a config reload is accepted) is its`HookKind::Output`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [HOOK_](https://docs.rs/constant.HOOK_MANAGER_ID.html)- MANAGER_ - ID
- The stable component id of the seeded `HookManager`
- [HOOK_](https://docs.rs/constant.HOOK_MANAGER_NAME.html)- MANAGER_ - NAME
- The display name of the seeded `HookManager`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentHooks.html)- Hooks
- A component type’s own hooks.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookKind.html)- Kind
- A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]`method reacts to.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookParam.html)- Param
- A parameter a `#[hook(K)]`method may take: an input of kind`K`, extracted from the kind’s context — never a component dependency (those come through`&self`).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [no_](https://docs.rs/fn.no_hooks.html)- hooks
- The empty hooks slice for a type that declares none — the default carried by a
`ComponentDescriptor`.

---

# lib.rs - source

# overseerd_hooks/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! A general lifecycle/event **hook** system.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! A hook is an `async` method on a component or service, marked `#[hook(Kind)]`, that the
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! framework calls when an event of `Kind` occurs. `Kind` is a [`HookKind`] type that owns
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! the hook's *output* (what the method returns) and its *context* (the typed inputs an
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! invocation carries). Built-in kinds are [`Startup`] and [`Shutdown`]; config reload is a
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! kind defined in `overseerd-config`. The system is deliberately general so user-defined
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! event kinds can be added the same way.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! Hooks do **not** receive component dependencies as parameters — those are reached through
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! `&self` (a hook may also be self-less). A hook's only parameters are the kind's inputs,
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! each a [`HookParam`] extracted from the kind's context. Hooks are collected per type
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! (the `{Type}Hooks` distributed slice, exposed via [`ComponentHooks`]) and registered into
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! a [`HookManager`]; a type with no hooks contributes nothing at runtime.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! This crate is generic over the [`ResolverCtx`](overseerd_core::ResolverCtx): a hook's
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! erased [`HookCall`] resolves its receiver through the resolver context, so the hook
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! layer never names the DI container (which sits above it).
[19](https://docs.rs#19)
[20](https://docs.rs#20)mod error;
[21](https://docs.rs#21)mod lifecycle;
[22](https://docs.rs#22)
[23](https://docs.rs#23)pub use error::{Error, Result};
[24](https://docs.rs#24)pub use lifecycle::{Shutdown, Startup};
[25](https://docs.rs#25)
[26](https://docs.rs#26)use std::any::{Any, TypeId};
[27](https://docs.rs#27)use std::collections::HashMap;
[28](https://docs.rs#28)use std::fmt;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)use std::future::Future;
[30](https://docs.rs#30)use std::pin::Pin;
[31](https://docs.rs#31)use std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};
[32](https://docs.rs#32)
[33](https://docs.rs#33)use overseerd_core::{DependencyDescriptor, ResolverCtx, TypeDescriptor};
[34](https://docs.rs#34)
[35](https://docs.rs#35)/// A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]` method reacts to.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)///
[37](https://docs.rs#37)/// The kind owns the contract: `Output` is what each hook of this kind returns (the kind
[38](https://docs.rs#38)/// "decides what output it needs"), and `Cx` is the owned, per-invocation context its
[39](https://docs.rs#39)/// parameters are extracted from (e.g. the proposed config values for a reload).
[40](https://docs.rs#40)pub trait HookKind: 'static {
[41](https://docs.rs#41)    /// A stable name for diagnostics and indexing.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)    const NAME: &'static str;
[43](https://docs.rs#43)
[44](https://docs.rs#44)    /// What each hook of this kind returns and the runner collects.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    type Output: Send + 'static;
[46](https://docs.rs#46)
[47](https://docs.rs#47)    /// The owned context one invocation carries, that this kind's [`HookParam`]s read.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    /// `Send + Sync` so the hook future (which borrows it) stays `Send`.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    type Cx: Send + Sync + 'static;
[50](https://docs.rs#50)}
[51](https://docs.rs#51)
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// A parameter a `#[hook(K)]` method may take: an input of kind `K`, extracted from the
[53](https://docs.rs#53)/// kind's context — never a component dependency (those come through `&self`).
[54](https://docs.rs#54)pub trait HookParam<K: HookKind>: Sized {
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    /// The dependency edge this parameter contributes, for validation and event routing
[56](https://docs.rs#56)    /// (e.g. the config path a reload hook targets). `path` is the param's `#[config("..")]`
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    /// literal, or `None` for the by-type shorthand.
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    fn dependency(path: Option<&'static str>) -> DependencyDescriptor;
[59](https://docs.rs#59)
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    /// Extracts this parameter from the kind's context.
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    fn extract(cx: &K::Cx, path: Option<&'static str>) -> Result<Self>;
[62](https://docs.rs#62)}
[63](https://docs.rs#63)
[64](https://docs.rs#64)/// The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method
[65](https://docs.rs#65)/// takes `&self`) from the resolver context, extract the kind's params from the erased
[66](https://docs.rs#66)/// context, run the method, and box its output. The boxed value is always the kind's
[67](https://docs.rs#67)/// `Output`.
[68](https://docs.rs#68)///
[69](https://docs.rs#69)/// The call takes `&dyn ResolverCtx` (not the container itself), so the hook layer stays
[70](https://docs.rs#70)/// below the DI engine. The macro-generated body resolves the receiver through the
[71](https://docs.rs#71)/// component source it fetches from the context.
[72](https://docs.rs#72)pub type HookCall =
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    for<'a> fn(
[74](https://docs.rs#74)        &'a (dyn ResolverCtx + Send + Sync),
[75](https://docs.rs#75)        &'a (dyn Any + Send + Sync),
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn Any + Send>>> + Send + 'a>>;
[77](https://docs.rs#77)
[78](https://docs.rs#78)/// Static metadata for one hook, registered into its type's `{Type}Hooks` slice.
[79](https://docs.rs#79)#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
[80](https://docs.rs#80)pub struct HookDescriptor {
[81](https://docs.rs#81)    /// The component/service the hook is defined on.
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    pub component_ty: TypeDescriptor,
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    /// The hook kind's [`NAME`](HookKind::NAME), for diagnostics.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    pub kind: &'static str,
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    /// `TypeId::of::<Kind>()`, used to select hooks of a given kind at runtime.
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    pub kind_ty: fn() -> TypeId,
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    /// The hook's parameter edges (kind inputs), reported at runtime for validation and
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    /// event routing.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    pub dependencies: fn() -> Vec<DependencyDescriptor>,
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    /// The erased call.
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    pub call: HookCall,
[92](https://docs.rs#92)}
[93](https://docs.rs#93)
[94](https://docs.rs#94)impl fmt::Debug for HookDescriptor {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[96](https://docs.rs#96)        f.debug_struct("HookDescriptor")
[97](https://docs.rs#97)            .field("component_ty", &self.component_ty)
[98](https://docs.rs#98)            .field("kind", &self.kind)
[99](https://docs.rs#99)            .field("dependencies", &(self.dependencies)())
[100](https://docs.rs#100)            .finish_non_exhaustive()
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    }
[102](https://docs.rs#102)}
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// A component type's own hooks.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// Implemented for each `#[component]`/`#[service]` by the macro to return that type's
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// `{Type}Hooks` distributed slice — the slice every `#[hook]` method appends to. The owning
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// `ComponentDescriptor` stores this as a fn pointer, so the registry reaches a type's hooks
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// without holding its type.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)pub trait ComponentHooks {
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    /// Every hook contributed to this type.
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    fn hooks() -> &'static [HookDescriptor];
[113](https://docs.rs#113)}
[114](https://docs.rs#114)
[115](https://docs.rs#115)/// The empty hooks slice for a type that declares none — the default carried by a
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// `ComponentDescriptor`.
[117](https://docs.rs#117)pub fn no_hooks() -> &'static [HookDescriptor] {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    &[]
[119](https://docs.rs#119)}
[120](https://docs.rs#120)
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// Runs hooks of a kind against the live component instances.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)///
[123](https://docs.rs#123)/// Built once at application build from every registered component's hook slice (empties
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// skipped), so it can be seeded as a framework singleton. The resolver context is attached
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// after the root scope is built (see [`attach`](Self::attach)).
[126](https://docs.rs#126)#[derive(Clone)]
[127](https://docs.rs#127)pub struct HookManager {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    inner: Arc<HookManagerInner>,
[129](https://docs.rs#129)}
[130](https://docs.rs#130)
[131](https://docs.rs#131)struct HookManagerInner {
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    ctx: OnceLock<Arc<dyn ResolverCtx + Send + Sync>>,
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    /// Hooks indexed by kind `TypeId`, so a kind with no listeners is an O(1) miss and a
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    /// fire over it does no work at all.
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    by_kind: HashMap<TypeId, Vec<HookDescriptor>>,
[136](https://docs.rs#136)}
[137](https://docs.rs#137)
[138](https://docs.rs#138)impl HookManager {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// Builds a manager over every registered hook (across all component types), grouped by
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// kind for O(1) listener lookup.
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    pub fn new(hooks: Vec<HookDescriptor>) -> Self {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)        let mut by_kind: HashMap<TypeId, Vec<HookDescriptor>> = HashMap::new();
[143](https://docs.rs#143)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)        for hook in hooks {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            by_kind.entry((hook.kind_ty)()).or_default().push(hook);
[146](https://docs.rs#146)        }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)
[148](https://docs.rs#148)        Self {
[149](https://docs.rs#149)            inner: Arc::new(HookManagerInner {
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                ctx: OnceLock::new(),
[151](https://docs.rs#151)                by_kind,
[152](https://docs.rs#152)            }),
[153](https://docs.rs#153)        }
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    }
[155](https://docs.rs#155)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    /// Attaches the resolver context, once it exists. Hooks resolve their `&self` receiver
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    /// through it. Idempotent; a second attach is ignored.
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    pub fn attach(&self, ctx: Arc<dyn ResolverCtx + Send + Sync>) {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)        let _ = self.inner.ctx.set(ctx);
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    /// Whether any hook of kind `K` is registered — an O(1) check a firing site uses to
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    /// skip building the event entirely when nothing listens.
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    pub fn has<K: HookKind>(&self) -> bool {
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        self.inner.by_kind.contains_key(&TypeId::of::<K>())
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    }
[167](https://docs.rs#167)
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    /// Runs every hook of kind `K` for which `filter` returns true, against `cx`,
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    /// **concurrently**, and collects each component's typed outcome (or error) in
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    /// registration order. Returns an empty `Vec` (no work) when nothing listens.
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    pub async fn run<K: HookKind>(
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        &self,
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        cx: &K::Cx,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        filter: impl Fn(&HookDescriptor) -> bool,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    ) -> Vec<(TypeDescriptor, Result<K::Output>)> {
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        let Some(bucket) = self.inner.by_kind.get(&TypeId::of::<K>()) else {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            return Vec::new();
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        };
[179](https://docs.rs#179)
[180](https://docs.rs#180)        let ctx = self
[181](https://docs.rs#181)            .inner
[182](https://docs.rs#182)            .ctx
[183](https://docs.rs#183)            .get()
[184](https://docs.rs#184)            .expect("hook manager resolver context attached before hooks run");
[185](https://docs.rs#185)
[186](https://docs.rs#186)        let calls = bucket.iter().filter(|hook| filter(hook)).map(|hook| {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)            let component = hook.component_ty;
[188](https://docs.rs#188)
[189](https://docs.rs#189)            async move {
[190](https://docs.rs#190)                let outcome = (hook.call)(ctx.as_ref(), cx as &(dyn Any + Send + Sync))
[191](https://docs.rs#191)                    .await
[192](https://docs.rs#192)                    .map(|boxed| {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)                        *boxed
[194](https://docs.rs#194)                            .downcast::<K::Output>()
[195](https://docs.rs#195)                            .expect("hook output type matches its kind")
[196](https://docs.rs#196)                    });
[197](https://docs.rs#197)
[198](https://docs.rs#198)                (component, outcome)
[199](https://docs.rs#199)            }
[200](https://docs.rs#200)        });
[201](https://docs.rs#201)
[202](https://docs.rs#202)        futures::future::join_all(calls).await
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    }
[204](https://docs.rs#204)}
[205](https://docs.rs#205)
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// The stable component id of the seeded [`HookManager`] singleton.
[207](https://docs.rs#207)pub const HOOK_MANAGER_ID: &str = "overseerd:hook-manager";
[208](https://docs.rs#208)
[209](https://docs.rs#209)/// The display name of the seeded [`HookManager`] singleton.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)pub const HOOK_MANAGER_NAME: &str = "HookManager";

# HookKind in overseerd_hooks - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-hooks/0.9.0/overseerd_hooks/trait.HookKind.html

```
pub trait HookKind: 'static {
    type
```
[Output](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Output): [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'static;
    type [Cx](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Cx): [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) + 'static;
    const [NAME](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.NAME): &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html);
}## Expand description

A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]` method reacts to.

The kind owns the contract: `Output` is what each hook of this kind returns (the kind
“decides what output it needs”), and `Cx` is the owned, per-invocation context its
parameters are extracted from (e.g. the proposed config values for a reload).

## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Startup in overseerd_hooks - Rust

`pub struct Startup;`## Expand description

Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving. An `Err` from any
`#[hook(Startup)]` aborts startup — the daemon does not begin accepting work.

# ComponentHooks in overseerd_hooks - Rust

pub trait ComponentHooks {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[hooks](https://docs.rs#tymethod.hooks)() -> &'static [[HookDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.HookDescriptor.html)];
}## Expand description

A component type’s own hooks.

Implemented for each `#[component]`/`#[service]` by the macro to return that type’s
`{Type}Hooks` distributed slice — the slice every `#[hook]` method appends to. The owning
`ComponentDescriptor` stores this as a fn pointer, so the registry reaches a type’s hooks
without holding its type.

# HookManager in overseerd_hooks - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-hooks/0.9.0/overseerd_hooks/struct.HookManager.html

`pub struct HookManager { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Runs hooks of a kind against the live component instances.

Built once at application build from every registered component’s hook slice (empties
skipped), so it can be seeded as a framework singleton. The resolver context is attached
after the root scope is built (see [ attach](https://docs.rs/struct.HookManager.html#method.attach)).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# ResolverCtx in overseerd_core::resolver - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-core/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_core/resolver/trait.ResolverCtx.html

## Expand description

A type-keyed set of [ Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.Resolver.html)s — the context an extractor resolves against.

Both the construction-time and request-time contexts implement this. It is
object-safe (keyed by [ TypeId](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/struct.TypeId.html), returning

`&dyn Any`), so it can be passed as
`&dyn ResolverCtx` — which is how a hook’s erased call reaches the component source
without the hook layer naming the container.## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# HookCall in overseerd_hooks - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd-hooks/0.9.0/overseerd_hooks/type.HookCall.html

`pub type HookCall = for<'a> `[fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html)(&'a (dyn [ResolverCtx](https://docs.rs/overseerd-core/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_core/resolver/trait.ResolverCtx.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)), &'a (dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html))) -> [Pin](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/pin/struct.Pin.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)>>> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'a>>;## Expand description

The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method
takes `&self`) from the resolver context, extract the kind’s params from the erased
context, run the method, and box its output. The boxed value is always the kind’s
`Output`.

The call takes `&dyn ResolverCtx` (not the container itself), so the hook layer stays
below the DI engine. The macro-generated body resolves the receiver through the
component source it fetches from the context.

---

# awsm-renderer-scene 0.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/awsm-renderer-scene/0.13.0

# awsm-renderer-scene

The lean, canonical **runtime** scene schema for the awsm-renderer player: a
`Scene` (`scene.toml`) plus an `assets/` directory, all referenced by id. The
player and renderer touch only this crate.

Coordinate convention: right-handed, Y-up, meters. Rotations are unit quaternions
stored as `[x, y, z, w]`.

## What's here

The on-disk types for everything a baked scene contains, each in its own module and re-exported at the crate root:

- Structure — `scene`,`tree`,`transform`,`instances`,`project_dir`.
- Renderables — `mesh`,`primitive`,`material`,`dynamic_material`,`sprite`,`line`,`decal`,`particle`.
- Stage — `light`,`shadows`,`camera`,`environment`.
- Motion / misc — `animation`,`curve`,`collider`.
- `assets`— the by-id asset table (- `scene.toml`+- `assets/<id>.*`).

## What's not here

Authoring. The modifier stack, per-vertex overrides, and the editor's
`Mesh = base + edits` model live in `awsm-renderer-meshgen` (recipe types) and
`awsm-renderer-editor-protocol` (the `EditorProject` document + `EditorCommand` /
`EditorQuery`), which depend on this crate and reuse its core types. The editor's
bake step lowers authoring → runtime (`MeshDef` → `mesh::MeshBlob`).

## Companion crates

- `awsm-renderer-scene-loader`— loads a runtime bundle described by this schema into the renderer.
- `awsm-renderer-editor-protocol`— the authoring layer that bakes down to this schema.

---

# awsm-renderer-scene 0.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/awsm-renderer-scene/0.13.0/source/

#
                    awsm-renderer-scene 0.13.0

                Lean canonical runtime scene schema (scene.toml + assets/) for the awsm-renderer player. Authoring types live in awsm-renderer-editor-protocol.
